name: Clocked
tagline: Know what your hours really earn
about: Clocked turns a freelancer's messy time log into the truth: your effective hourly rate per client, which projects were underquoted, where non-billable hours leak, and better estimates for the next job.
persona: You are a numbers-first freelance profitability analyst: you show the arithmetic, name the worst client by the data, and suggest one change at a time.

onboarding.title: Every hour, accounted for
onboarding.subtitle: Your target rate turns time logs into verdicts.

tools.title: Analyse my time log
tools.subtitle: Paste hours, get the truth

inputs.label: Time log
inputs.placeholder: Client A: 22h, paid 1200; Client B: 40h, paid 1800; admin 9h; marketing 5h

tools.prompt: Analyse this time log for '{period}': {log}. Produce a table (Client/Project | Hours | Paid | Effective rate | vs profile target), a kv (total hours, billable %, blended effective rate, hours worked below target, best and worst client), bullets with the 3 findings that matter most, and a callout with the single change that would raise the blended rate most next period.

tools.title: Estimate the next job
tools.subtitle: From your own history

inputs.label: The new job
inputs.placeholder: 2-min brand film, 2 shoot days, motion graphics

tools.prompt: Using this history: {history}, estimate the new job: {new}. Produce a table (Phase | Low hours | Likely hours | High hours | Basis from history), a kv (likely total hours, price at the profile target rate, price with 15% contingency, suggested fixed price), a text section on the assumptions and what would blow the estimate, and a callout on the questions to ask before committing to a number.

tools.title: Timesheet → invoice lines
tools.subtitle: Group, round, describe

inputs.label: Raw entries
inputs.placeholder: Mon 1.2h edit v2; Tue 0.4 call; Tue 2.1 colour grade; Wed 0.3 email…

tools.prompt: Convert these entries: {entries} into invoice lines using '{rounding}' rounding. Produce a table (Line | Description written for the client | Hours | Amount at the profile rate) grouped by task type, a kv (raw total, rounded total, difference), bullets of entries you'd consider non-billable or should flag to the client before billing, and a callout on describing work as outcomes rather than activities.

tools.title: Non-billable audit
tools.subtitle: Where the unpaid hours go

inputs.label: Your unpaid hours last month
inputs.placeholder: invoicing 4h, proposals 9h, calls with no-shows 3h, tool fiddling 6h

tools.prompt: Audit these unpaid hours: {admin}. Produce a table (Activity | Hours | Cost at the profile target rate | Cut, automate, delegate or bill?), steps to reclaim the biggest 3 in order of effort, a kv of the monthly value recovered if the plan works, and a callout on the unpaid hours that are actually investments and should stay.

tools.title: Time to raise my rate?
tools.subtitle: Signals from the data

inputs.label: Recent signals
inputs.placeholder: 3 inquiries turned away, no pushback on quotes since spring

tools.prompt: Utilisation: {utilisation}%. Signals: {signals}. Give a text verdict on whether to raise the profile target rate and by roughly how much, a table (Signal | Points to a raise? | Weight) with the evidence, a kv (proposed new rate, expected client churn range, break-even churn so income stays flat), and a callout on sequencing: new clients first, existing clients with notice.

disclaimer: Not financial or tax advice; figures are estimates based on what you enter.
